Hello, my sister is a physical therapist. This is usually what's done.

  • For the pain put on a numbing agent like this http://www.physioroom.com/images/products//full/37766_image.jpg. Doesn't have to be that brand, but an equivalent to it. These come in gel form as well. This will numb the pain. You might have to experiment to see which helps you the most. If you use a gel, rub it in with a glove. You don't want that on your hand.

  • Second, compress the shoulder. They have fabric devices that will do compression.

Example: http://www.klika.com.au/shoulder-sports-injury-compression-support.html

  • Third, take the advice of your doctor. Tape your arm down to reduce movement of the shoulder. Do not do light weights. Get some sports tape, and tape that shit down.

  • Fourth, yes, put some heat on it. A hot water bottle is suitable, but they have a variety of products that can do this. There are bags that can be heated in a microwave. I have one called a Magic Bag.

And that's it really. Stop moving your arm around, because you are delaying the healing process.
